title: ChatGPT Starts Reading Your Medical Records
hook: OpenAI has shipped Health in ChatGPT: eligible US users can connect their medical records and Apple Health data so the assistant answers from their own history rather than in general.
key_points: Health in ChatGPT launched 23 July 2026, initially for eligible users in the United States.
Users can connect medical records and Apple Health data to the assistant.
OpenAI frames the goal as more personalized insights and better understanding of one's own health.
It moves ChatGPT from answering general health questions to reasoning over an individual's own record.
Connecting a health record is a consequential data decision — the assistant's context now holds regulated personal data.
content_html: OpenAI has launched Health in ChatGPT, which lets eligible users in the United States connect their medical records and Apple Health data to the assistant. The pitch is personalization: instead of general answers about a condition, the model reasons over your actual history.
extra_html:
Why this one is worth noticing

Most assistant features add capability. This one adds data — and specifically the most sensitive category of personal data most people have. The interesting questions are less about model quality than about plumbing and consent: what gets pulled into context, how long it persists, who can see it, and how a general-purpose model behaves when it is confidently wrong about something clinical.

It also marks a direction of travel. Connecting authoritative personal records is the same move behind assistants reading your email, calendar, and files — the assistant becomes useful in proportion to how much of your life it can see, and risky for exactly the same reason. Announced by OpenAI, 23 July 2026.
